title: Routed econ decomposer with causal span tracing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a deterministic, low-latency service that computes per-request cost and latency attributions broken down by route, model variant, and customer. This ticket implements a new decomposition approach that uses causal-span tracing (propagated across front-end, router, runtime, quantization and fallback steps) to attribute tokens and micro-latency to the correct entity, even for complex batched and multi-model requests.

Why this is different: existing rollups conflate batched kernel time and prefix-cache hits, producing noisy per-route economics. Our approach ties measured GPU/kernel spans back to the incoming route/model via deterministic crediting windows plus probabilistic split heuristics for ambiguous cases (e.g., shared batch kernels and mixed-tenant host lanes). This hybrid model improves explainability while remaining computationally cheap for the nightly rollups and realtime sampling indexes.

High-level design:
- Ingest: extended trace/span metadata emitted by runtime (span ids, parent ids, model_variant, request_route, customer_id, token_count, kv_cache_hit_flags, batch_slot_id). We will add a small routing header to requests so downstream runtime can tag spans.
- Attribution engine: a service that consumes spans (Kafka topic: runtime-spans-v2) and converts server-side spans into atomic attributions: token-level cost tokens (microtokens), kernel-time-ms, network-ms, and cache-hit credit. Attribution rules are declarative and versioned (git + JSON schema).
- Deterministic rules: when a span has an explicit route and model_variant we attribute 100% to that pair. For batch-shared spans (single kernel invocation covering multiple requests) we use batch_slot_id to split deterministic tokens when slot mapping is available.
- Probabilistic splitting: when no slot mapping exists (legacy lanes or cross-tenant batching), we fall back to a weighted probabilistic split using request sizes, historical per-tenant token distribution, and model-specific per-token throughput. The fallback is recorded with a confidence score.
- Causal adjustments: handle retries and fallback model calls by linking spans via a causal-chain table to avoid double-charging. Example: a request that tried model A then fell back to model B will have cost attributed to the successful model B and a separate trace entry for the failed attempt with zero-retry charge policy per product rules.
- Output: per-minute and per-request attributions written to two sinks: (1) realtime topic runtime-attributions-realtime (for Console latency views and alerts), (2) hourly compact parquet batches in S3 for downstream rollups and billing ingestion. Each attribution record includes reason codes and confidence.

Storage & Schema: attribution records follow a compact flat schema (no nested JSON) compatible with the console ledger. Sample columns: timestamp, request_id, customer_id, route, model_variant, microtokens, kernel_ms, network_ms, cache_hits, attribution_reason, confidence_score, source_span_id. Schema changes are managed via SQL migrations and a central schema registry.

SLOs and performance constraints: the realtime service must process 99th of incoming spans with <200ms added processing latency and maintain <5% extra compute cost compared to current rollups. End-to-end nightly rollup compute should increase <15% for typical tenant volumes.

Rollout plan: 
1) Prototype on a 5% sampling lane, emit enriched spans and run attribution in parallel (read-only) to validate differences against the legacy rollup.
2) Run offline reconciliation for 2 weeks, produce drift dashboards and flagged accounts where confidence <0.6.
3) Gradual traffic migration per region with feature flag.
4) Finalize schema and flip for realtime ingestion and billing downstream.

Testing & QA: unit tests for deterministic and probabilistic split logic, integration tests with synthetic runtime traces (mixed batch sizes, retries, multi-model flows). A small canary of production traffic will run with a shadow-writer that compares outputs. We'll add an E2E regression suite that asserts monotonicity (total-cost before/after within expected deltas) and no double counting for retries.

Operational concerns & telemetry: dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/route-econ-decomposer (proto). Ship metrics: attribution-latency-p50/p95, attribution-reconciles, probabilistic-splits-rate, confidence-distribution. Add alerts for surge in probabilistic splits and significant drift (>10%) vs legacy rollup.

Artifacts & references: design notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFR/Routed+Econ+Decomposer, proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12567, Kafka topics and ACLs documented in infra runbook.

Open decisions: how aggressively to penalize failed model attempts (currently configured to zero-charge but Product wants 10% charged if failure reason is non-resource). We need PM signoff. Also need agreement with Billing on confidence_score semantics for invoicing.

Next steps: finalize attribution rule schema, complete runtime span tagging (ENG-727940), deploy prototype sampler, and sync with Billing/PM for confidence semantics.

2025-02-27 - Infra review (Rajiv Mehta): Kafka ACLs approved for runtime-spans-v2 and runtime-attributions-realtime. Noted that topic retention must be 72h for tracing replay during incidents.

2025-03-01 - Data QA (Nora Kim): Ran reconciliation job comparing new attributions vs legacy rollup on a 1M-request sample. Median delta in kernel_ms attribution is -1.8% but some skew for small-batch GPU shared kernels. Creating a follow-up optimization ticket to tighten slot mapping accuracy.
